entries.mechanism: Severe neuromuscular blockade; profound inhibition of postsynaptic nicotinic acetylcholine receptors.
entries.clinicalPearl: Absolute contraindication in Myasthenia Gravis. Can precipitate rapid, fatal myasthenic crisis within hours of the first dose.
safeInpatientAlternatives: Respiratory Fluoroquinolones (Note: also high risk for MG; use beta-lactams if possible)

entries.mechanism: Irreversible inhibition of presynaptic acetylcholine release at the neuromuscular junction.
entries.clinicalPearl: Even localized cosmetic, spasticity, or migraine injections can trigger severe systemic bulbar and respiratory weakness in MG patients.
safeInpatientAlternatives: Non-botulinum oral spasticity agents (baclofen, tizanidine) used cautiously

entries.mechanism: D-penicillamine induces autoimmune anti-AChR antibody production (de novo MG). Quinine directly impairs neuromuscular transmission.
entries.clinicalPearl: Avoid D-penicillamine entirely in genetically predisposed patients. Quinine for nocturnal cramps is strictly contraindicated.
safeInpatientAlternatives: Magnesium supplementation / non-pharmacologic stretching for nocturnal cramps

entries.mechanism: Direct postsynaptic AChR blockade and chelation of presynaptic calcium channels.
entries.clinicalPearl: Frequent inpatient crisis trigger when ordered empirically for UTI or pneumonia in the ED. Monitor respiratory parameters closely if mandatory.

entries.mechanism: Impair presynaptic acetylcholine release by blocking calcium influx into nerve terminals.
entries.clinicalPearl: High risk of inducing acute weakness. If essential for resistant gram-negative sepsis, require ICU monitoring and PLEX readiness.
Commonly ordered for atypical CAP. Can precipitate acute bulbar and limb weakness within 24-72 hours.

entries.mechanism: Competitively blocks calcium entry at presynaptic nerve terminals, inhibiting acetylcholine release.
entries.clinicalPearl: Major inpatient trap when primary teams aggressively replete mild asymptomatic hypomagnesemia or treat preeclampsia. Check serum magnesium and keep levels normal-low strict.

entries.mechanism: T-cell activation unmasking autoimmune responses against neuromuscular junction antigens.
entries.clinicalPearl: Can precipitate fulminant de novo MG or catastrophic exacerbations, frequently overlapping with myositis and myocarditis ('triple M syndrome').
safeInpatientAlternatives: Consult oncology and neuro-immunology prior to holding or continuing immunotherapy; immediate high-dose steroids and PLEX if weakness emerges.

entries.mechanism: Direct membrane stabilization and interference with neuromuscular transmission.
entries.clinicalPearl: Systemic beta-blockers and ophthalmic timolol drops can unmask mild subclinical MG. Use cardioselective agents or alternative antihypertensives (ACEi/ARBs/CCBs) if possible.
